title: UIAO Substrate Manifest Schema
description: Schema for the top-level substrate manifest that declares the modules, roles, principles, and drift-scan scope of the UIAO monorepo.

principles.description: Universal substrate principles that apply at all ADR-076 conformance tiers. Per ADR-079 the canonical set is SSOT, Canon-anchored evidence, and Drift is explicit. The customer Governance OS Executive Brief cites this section as the principle authority. Code-is-SSOT per ADR-079.

tier_specific_principles.description: Principles that apply only at named ADR-076 conformance tiers. Per ADR-079 the canonical set is Two-Brain Execution (Tier 3+), Boundary Enforcement (Tier 4+), and Tenant Agnosticism (Tier 5). Promoted from the canon /customer-documents/reference-architecture/ narrative; the other 4 canon-narrative principles (Deterministic State, Schema Fixity, Provenance Traceability, Drift Resistance) collapse into the universal 3 per ADR-079's mapping.

root_env.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the absolute workspace root path. Never hardcode the path value itself.

fallbacks.description: Documented platform-specific fallback examples. Informational only; runtime MUST read the env var.

root.description: Canonical GitHub URL for the monorepo.

sub_boundaries.description: Optional sub-boundaries inside a top-level module.

classes.description: Drift classes the manifest declares itself subject to. Full taxonomy defined in docs/docs/16_DriftDetectionStandard.qmd.

roots.description: Module paths that the drift detector walks when validating the substrate.

orgtree_readiness_schema.description: Path to OrgTree readiness bundle schema (UIAO_006/007 OrgTree modernization). Added in v0.6.0.

retired_slugs.description: Slugs that have been renamed by an ADR. The substrate walker scans canon/ and docs/ for any literal occurrence of `slug` and emits a P2 DRIFT-PROVENANCE advisory naming the `replacement`. Optional `rationale` is surfaced in the finding detail. The intended workflow is: an ADR retires a slug, adds an entry here, and the walker keeps subsequent PRs honest by flagging any drift back to the old name.

slug.description: The retired slug (e.g., `MOD_A`). Matched as a literal with word boundaries.

replacement.description: The current canonical slug that replaces it (e.g., `UIAO_151`).

rationale.description: Short citation of the ADR or PR that retired the slug (e.g., `ADR-060`).

description.description: Operative declaration of what the principle requires.

source_authority.description: Optional ADR or canon doc citation establishing the principle.

description.description: Operative declaration of what the principle requires.

tier.description: ADR-076 conformance tier at which this principle becomes operational.

tier_inclusive.description: If true (default), the principle applies at the named tier AND all higher tiers. If false, applies only at exactly that tier.

rationale.description: Why the principle applies at this specific tier and not at lower tiers.

source_authority.description: Optional ADR or canon doc citation establishing the principle.

name.description: Module identifier (matches the top-level directory name).

path.description: Repo-relative path to the module root.

role.description: Module role. Post-ADR-032 the canonical set is: authority (defines canon), consumer (derives from canon), package (single installable distribution carrying both canon and code), tooling (workspace scripts), staging (draft surface — not canon), deploy (deployment artifacts).

canon_consumer.description: True if the module derives artifacts from canon (see src/uiao/rules/canon-consumer.md).
